title: Align quest agents --check with DEC-238 (a6): override, coverage and reachability lines, byte-for-byte with the lore-cli LCLI-765 wording
description:
Follow-up to QCLI-531, from DEC-238 (a6), opum-doc ruling 2026-10-25T13:19:22Z (record: opum-ai/opum-doc PR on chore/dec-238-a6), relayed by the lead. QCLI-531 landed (#678) before (a6) arrived and shipped `stateScope: "managed-block"`, which is NOT the (a6) wording.

(a6) requires quest to adopt the SAME wording lore-cli is building for LCLI-765, so QCLI-371/381 byte-for-byte agreement holds:
1. The remedy names the scope where the override LIVES (`--scope local` for .claude/settings.local.json, `project` for .claude/settings.json, `user` for a user-scope disable), never a fixed scope. [Implemented on the branch; proved by test and mutation.]
2. `plugin-claude-override <file> (<scope> scope) sets opum-quest@opum to disabled, and wins over the user-scope row`, plus an additive JSON field. [Exact bytes to be agreed with lore-cli.]
3. `agents-coverage up-to-date covers the managed block and the skill file only, not plugin enablement`. [Exact quest phrasing to be agreed: quest state word is `current`, not `up-to-date`.]
4. `agents-skill-reachability ...`, where it applies to quest: no quest skill is expected by design under DEC-238 (a3) and DEC-172 (4bf), which differs from lore reaching no skill at all.

`stateScope: "managed-block"` (shipped in #678) stays only if (a6) lines are added beside it; if the coverage line carries the same statement, removing `stateScope` is part of this work. That call is settled with lore-cli in the same exchange.

COORDINATION: lore-cli (LCLI-765) owns the same lines for opum-lore@opum; one PR per repository. Bytes must be identical modulo the plugin id and any quest-specific vocabulary lore-cli and opum-doc agree. Nothing is invented here: an unconfirmed string that lands becomes the contract.

RELEASE/MERGE: this PR does NOT merge on green. The next leader spawns a reviewer unit and clears the merge. No release.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The remedy prints the scope where the override lives (local, project, or user) and never a fixed scope; proved by a test that fails when the listing row scope is used instead
The plugin-claude-override line and its additive JSON field carry bytes agreed verbatim with lore-cli (LCLI-765), with only the plugin id and any agreed quest vocabulary differing
The agents-coverage line is present with the agreed bytes, and stateScope is either removed or kept beside it per the agreement recorded on this task
The agents-skill-reachability line is present with the agreed bytes for quest, or its omission is recorded with the reason lore-cli and opum-doc gave
The exit code is unchanged by any of these lines (DEC-238 (a5))
The agreed bytes and the exchange that fixed them are recorded on this task before the PR is offered for review

implementationNotes:
BYTES AGREED with lore-cli, 2026-10-25, against their implementation in opum-ai/lore-cli#678 and their reply on LCLI-765. Their answers, recorded so the wording cannot be reconstructed differently later:

1. Override line, their literal bytes: "plugin-claude-override <file> (<scope> scope) sets opum-lore@opum to disabled, and wins over the user-scope row", with the plugin id swapped and nothing else. <file> is checkout-relative and forward-slashed; the parenthetical is literally (local scope) or (project scope). In --plain it is its own record, placed after the plugin-claude <state> line and before plugin-claude-remedy; the human view prints the same sentence indented under the state line.
2. JSON: they are renaming theirs to match this PR — lore will emit override: {scope, file} on the plugin check, additive, absent when no file overrides. scope on the report stays the runtime reported install scope; only the remedy --scope follows the override.
3. Coverage line: lore bytes "agents-coverage up-to-date covers the managed block and the skill file only, not plugin enablement"; their reading (not a ruling) is that each CLI names its own verdict word, so quest says current. Adopted: "agents-coverage current covers the managed block and the skill file only, not plugin enablement".
4. Reachability line: lore fires it only when skill_source is plugin, no per-repo SKILL.md exists, and the plugin is disabled or not installed. Quest has no skill-source concept, so nothing is ruled for quest and lore-cli explicitly said do not invent a phrasing: it goes to opum-doc through team-lead. Not implemented.
5. Placement: coverage and reachability are human/--plain only, no JSON field, only on runs that report plugin state. The only JSON field in this set is override.

IMPLEMENTED: the override sentence and the coverage sentence are printed as their own trailing records in the human and --plain views of `quest agents`, never in --json; the JSON carries plugin.override = {file, scope} only. Placement diverges from lore by necessity: quest has no `plugin-claude <state>` line to sit after, because its human view is the structured dump, so both sentences follow the dump as their own records.

stateScope DECISION (mine, as lore-cli left it): the coverage sentence carries the same statement, so stateScope: "managed-block" is REMOVED rather than duplicated; the help detail that described it is replaced by a coverage entry.

Remedy scoping follows their reading: the override applies to a disabled row; a managed row still gets the managed remedy first.

Opus REQUEST_CHANGES on 66a3436 addressed on 5f0cf96f and f3fb35f5: override walk stops at the first boolean; override attached only to a disabled non-managed row and kept off the update path (no settings-writing command ever runs); (a9) 5-7 applied (override line before the dump, no precedence claim, remedy always --scope local). DEC-238 (a10), opum-ai/opum-doc#1371: the collaborator clause sits inside the one line for the project-file row only, byte-identical with lore-cli LCLI-766: plugin-claude-override .claude/settings.json (project scope) sets <plugin> to disabled for every collaborator, and is the effective setting in this checkout. Not done: finding 5 (settings read relative to cwd only); managed-row remedy text unchanged.

Managed row, DEC-238 (a9) 7: a disabled managed row now carries no command and the text "an administrator's managed setting disables it" (managedScopeDisabledRemedy); an installed managed row keeps the agreed managedScopeRemedy, since nothing there is disabled. (a10) bytes already in place on f3fb35f5 and pinned verbatim in test/qcli371.

RE-REVIEW VERDICT on PR #679 (squash-merged as 3a7f297c on dev), recorded verbatim at the lead's instruction, 2026-10-25. Unit quest-cli-review-679b, 48/48 turns claude-opus-5-5, SHA cbbfd7d5dd5f7cf25db06a6d6ec30e7eedcbe6a5, worktree .claude/worktrees/review-679-cbbfd7d, sha256 3690336bcf6d8ab8. Between the markers is the verdict file, unchanged.

VERDICT: APPROVE on opum-ai/quest-cli#679 (QCLI-532) at cbbfd7d5. Both causes of finding 1 are fixed, no override can reach an executed argv, and the remaining findings are non-blocking.

VERDICT: APPROVE
SHA: cbbfd7d5dd5f7cf25db06a6d6ec30e7eedcbe6a5

SCOPE:
- I read both diff files in full; both were readable. The full PR is 685 lines and the fix-only diff (66a3436...cbbfd7d5) is 550.
- Read in full at the worktree: src/adapters/agents/cli-agent-plugins.ts and src/application/agents/agent-plugins.ts.
- From src/cli/main.ts: output() (:204-255), renderAgentCheckLines (:324-362), the agents --check/--update path (:2400-2490), the init detection path (:2241-2256) and the `quest help agents` details (:2089-2107).
- From src/domain/agent-plugins.ts: printable, plainScope and questPluginUpdateSteps.
- From test/qcli381: the managed tests. Also the earlier verdict and QCLI-532.json.
- I grepped src/ for `.override` and `.list(`, and grepped /Volumes/external/repos (local checkouts) for both managed strings.

AUTHORING MODEL: re-measured, but by match counts, not by turns.
- Every `"model"` value in transcript 12ba4247 is `claude-sonnet-5-5` or `claude-opus-5-5`.
- The two opus hits are not authored turns: line 12 is the advisor-tool attachment and line 18 is the api-request-shape.
- `deepseek` appears only in tool-schema description text (lines 18 and 45) and in the quoted earlier verdict (line 78). It is never a model field.
- I count 84 lines matching `"type":"assistant"`. I cannot confirm the leader's 81/81 exactly, because -o match counts do not map one-to-one onto turns.
- I did not tie the fix commits to this transcript. That is under UNVERIFIED.
- The fix authoring meets DEC-182 (1). The DeepSeek breach before 66a3436 stands as recorded, and this review is its remedy.

EARLIER FINDINGS:
- 1(a) FIXED, cli-agent-plugins.ts:298-301. The walk stops at the first file where `typeof enabled[id] === "boolean"` and returns an override only for `false`. Test: qcli371:466-485 (local true over project false gives no override, remedy `--scope user`). Its control, a project false alone giving a project override, is :431-464. Under the old `=== false` loop, :479 would go red.
- 1(b) FIXED, agent-plugins.ts:253-256. The override is attached only when `state === "disabled" && !managed`.
  - The executed-argv trace, end to end: main.ts:2466 calls updateQuestPlugin. That returns early unless the row is installed, non-managed and runtimeNamed (:285-294). Only then does it call `port.update(runtime, plainScope(detected.scope))` (:305), where the scope is the listing row's. The port then runs questPluginUpdateSteps (domain), which only ever builds `claude plugin update <id> [--scope <row scope>]`.
  - The override is not an input anywhere on that path. `claude plugin enable` is never built into any argv.
  - This holds structurally, not by convention. The adapter attaches `override` to every claude row unconditionally (cli-agent-plugins.ts:355-359), but grep shows exactly one reader of `row.override` (agent-plugins.ts:255, behind the gate) and one of `plugin.override` (main.ts:350, the renderer).
  - remedyFor uses `scope`, not the override-derived scope, for an installed row (:222). So even with the gate removed, the update argv would stay at the row scope.
  - Test: qcli371:487-516. The installed row carries a project false. It asserts the override is absent, the human view has no sentence, the fake-call log contains `claude plugin update opum-quest@opum --scope user`, and nothing with `--scope project` or `plugin enable` appears.
- 2 FIXED.
  - No settings file gives no override in --json, human or --plain: :550-560.
  - --json stdout carries neither sentence: :411-412 and :554.
  - --plain is asserted, with the order: :420-428.
  - A managed row with a local file disable: :518-548.
  - The update path: :487-516.
- 4 FIXED, cli-agent-plugins.ts:306-310. The class docblock now names readClaudeOverride as the one exception, under DEC-238 (a6) Q1, and says nothing there writes a settings file.
- 8 FIXED, CHANGELOG.md:38-52, under `## Unreleased` / `### Fixed`.

SECURITY (verified clean):
- No path executes a settings-writing command without an explicit user command. The `--scope local` enable remedy is only ever a printed string.
- The read is hardened. statSync follows symlinks, so a symlink to /dev/zero or a FIFO is not isFile and is skipped. Anything over 1 MiB is skipped. JSON.parse sits in try/catch, and isRecord guards both levels.
- Paths come from a constant table joined under root, so there is no traversal.
- override.file and override.scope come only from that table. The printed line uses the questPluginId constant. No file content reaches a printed string or argv, and none can escalate a scope.
- The stat-then-read TOCTOU gap is not exploitable by a committed file. A symlink to a readable regular file outside the repo is parsed and discarded, and none of its content is emitted.
- Exit codes are unchanged: the lines exist only on output()'s exit-0 path.

STRINGS:
- (a9) 6 matches byte for byte (main.ts:354-356): `plugin-claude-override <file> (<scope> scope) sets opum-quest@opum to disabled, and is the effective setting in this checkout`.
- (a10) matches byte for byte for the project row only (`override.scope === "project"` inserts " for every collaborator" before the comma). It is pinned verbatim at qcli371:455-457, and the local row asserts no "collaborator" (:418).
- (a9) 5: the line is printed BEFORE the dump, in human and --plain alike (output() main.ts:245 routes every non-json mode through the same renderer). So it precedes the remedy, as tested at :420-428.
- (a9) 7: a project disable gives `claude plugin enable opum-quest@opum --scope local` (:447-449), local gives `--scope local`, and user gives `--scope user`. A disabled managed row gives exactly "an administrator's managed setting disables it" with no `claude plugin` anywhere in stdout (:539-546).
- The writer's managed reading is SOUND. (a9) 7 is a list of DISABLING rows ("a disabling row in ... gets"), and "disables it" would be a false sentence on an installed managed row. Keeping managedScopeRemedy there is the faithful reading.
- managedScopeRemedy keeps a control both ways: qcli381:119-122 and :178-184 show an installed managed row still printing it, and qcli381:133-136, :200-203 and :215-218 show a disabled one printing the new text.

FINDINGS (all non-blocking):
1. agent-plugins.ts:95-99, new since 66a3436 and the same class as finding 4. The managedScopeRemedy docblock still says "One string for installed and disabled alike", and qcli381:101-102 says "One string for both states". Both are now false.
   - This splits a string agreed with lore-cli under LCLI-604.
   - My local lore-cli checkout's src/core/agent-plugins.ts:170-173 still carries one MANAGED_SCOPE_REMEDY "for both states", with no (a9) 7 text. Either the lore half has not landed in that checkout or lore has not split. Confirm with lore-cli (LCLI-766) that its disabled managed row prints the same (a9) 7 text before calling the pair byte-identical.
   - No opum-cli-e2e file contains either string, so nothing there pins the old one.
2. test qcli371:562-576 ("a non-regular settings file is not read") does not discriminate.
   - It uses a directory, and readFileSync throws EISDIR inside the try/catch anyway, so deleting the `isFile()` guard leaves it green.
   - The 1 MiB cap has no test at all.
   - Suggest a valid `{"enabledPlugins":{"opum-quest@opum":false}}` padded with whitespace past maxPluginOutputBytes, expecting no override. It goes red if the cap is removed. A FIFO would cover isFile.
3. main.ts:2255: `quest init` also calls detectQuestPlugin.
   - Its JSON now carries `plugins.claude.override` and the `--scope local` remedy without the explanatory override line.
   - CHANGELOG.md:38 names only `quest agents --check`.
   - It is printed only, so it is not a security issue. It is an undocumented surface.
4. main.ts:324-338: two consecutive JSDoc blocks. The first, which describes renderAgentCheckLines, now sits above `const overrideCollaboratorClause`, so tooling attaches it to the wrong symbol. Cosmetic.
5. (a9) 5 placement: the operative clause, "before the remedy", holds.
   - Quest prepends the line before the whole dump, and the test checks only `indexOf(override) < indexOf(remedy)`, which any prepend satisfies.
   - Earlier finding 6 described lore's line as sitting after `plugin-claude <state>`. Exact position relative to the state line is unverified against lore.
6. cli-agent-plugins.ts:355-359 re-stats and re-reads both files once per listed claude plugin, though only the opum-quest row is consumed. Trivial cost.
7. readClaudeOverride discards an explicit `true`. Take a user-scope disabled row beside a project-file true: quest reports disabled with remedy `--scope user`, while project-over-user precedence would make the plugin enabled.
   - This is pre-existing state derivation from the listing, and the failure is a harmless printed command.
   - Whether `claude plugin list --json` emits a per-scope row for project-file entries, which would already decide this, is unmeasured. It is for routing, not this round.

UNVERIFIED:
- I did not tie the full 66a3436..cbbfd7d5 commit list to transcript 12ba4247. With no shell I could not list the commits.
- CI on cbbfd7d5 was read by the leader, not by me. I ran no tests, check suite or mutations.
- The lore-cli side of (a9) 7 and (a10) was read only from a local checkout, which may lag origin.
- What `claude plugin list --json` reports for project/local settings-file entries.
- Re-confirmed from the earlier verdict and still open: what `claude plugin update --scope <row scope>` writes.
--- END VERDICT ---
finalSummary: PR #679, squash-merged as 3a7f297c on dev: quest agents --check names the Claude settings file that disables opum-quest (plugin.override in --json; plugin-claude-override and agents-coverage lines in human/--plain), per DEC-238 (a6), (a9) and (a10). Review: an Opus unit returned REQUEST_CHANGES at 66a3436 (override precedence, and an override reaching an executed update argv); both causes were fixed, (a9)/(a10) bytes applied, and a fresh Opus unit APPROVED cbbfd7d5 (verbatim above). Checked with evidence: AC 1 (remedy scope; a test fails on the listing row scope), AC 3, AC 5 (exit codes unchanged, tested and reviewed), AC 6. Left unchecked: AC 2 (lore-cli side of the byte match unconfirmed, the verdict read only a lagging local checkout; follow-up on QCLI-534 to confirm with LCLI-766), AC 4 (reachability line omitted per (a8) Q2, not restated here), DoD 2 (no mutation was run by me; the reviewer reasoned the old loop would go red), DoD 3 (the full local check was not green: bun 1.3.14 vs the pinned runtime and three mod tests that cannot resolve claude-code/testing; CI source-gates, Tracker integrity and lore check were green on cbbfd7d5). Non-blocking findings go to QCLI-534; findings 5 and 7 are routed to opum-doc.
